key_insight: A gradient Cr3C2-NiCr detonation coating delivered markedly better corrosion resistance than a homogeneous coating by creating a denser layered barrier structure.
engineering_relevance: Sequentially tuning detonation spray conditions can improve protective coating durability for steel components exposed to aggressive corrosive environments.
method: Applied Cr3C2-NiCr (75/25, 10–45 µm) onto 12Kh1MF steel using CCDS2000 detonation spraying.
Compared a homogeneous coating (constant 57% gas filling ratio) with a gradient coating (57 → 64 → 73%).
Evaluated microstructure, phase composition, potentiodynamic polarization in 3.5% Na2SO4, and 1000 h acid-mist exposure.
evidence_signal: The gradient coating shifted polarization curves to lower current densities, showed no visible corrosion after 1000 h, and had much lower mass loss than the homogeneous coating (0.17% vs 1.14%).
watch_item: Performance gains depend on precise control of spray parameters and layered integrity, so process repeatability and scale-up need verification.
paper_title: Study of the Corrosion Resistance of Cr3C2-NiCr-Based Gradient Detonation Coatings
